report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/council/canary.py chunk 3 of 5, lines 561-720. All docstring claims checked against visible code; several uncheckable due to out-of-chunk definitions.
risks: ProbeResult.__post_init__ | medium | Validates status and severity against CANARY_STATUSES and SEVERITIES which are defined outside this chunk; if those constants change, validation may not match actual usage. | Inspect definitions of CANARY_STATUSES and SEVERITIES in the rest of the file.

ProbeResult.asked | medium | Relies on status being exactly 'unavailable' to mean 'not asked'; any other non-ok status is treated as asked. If status vocabulary changes, this property may misclassify. | Check the full set of CANARY_STATUSES and how each status is assigned in the runner.

claims.text: ``--quick`` runs this one. It is the probe that would have caught both real incidents on day one, so if only one probe can be afforded, it is this one.
claims.why: The claim about catching real incidents is historical and not verifiable from code. The constant is defined as 'arrival' and probes_for uses it for quick mode, but the assertion about incidents is uncheckable.

claims.text: One (lane, probe) outcome. Carries WHICH check failed, not just that one did.
claims.why: ProbeResult has a failed_check field that records the name of the failed deterministic check.

claims.text: Empty when the checker was never reached.
claims.why: The field defaults to empty string and is only set when a check fails; the code does not populate it otherwise.
The reason field defaults to empty string; the comment indicates it is only filled for transport errors, which are not ok/wrong_answer. The code does not set it for those statuses.

claims.text: Did a prompt actually reach a model? ``unavailable`` means it did not.
claims.why: The property returns self.status != 'unavailable', so it is True for all statuses except 'unavailable'.

claims.text: Counts that keep "could not ask" apart from "answer was wrong". ``asked`` and ``could_not_ask`` are separate top-level keys and ``by_status`` reports every member of the closed vocabulary individually. There is deliberately no combined "failures" number: a single number is exactly where the two get merged.
claims.why: summary returns separate keys 'asked' and 'could_not_ask', and by_status counts each status individually. There is no combined 'failures' key.

claims.text: Non-zero only when a previously-passing LIVENESS probe now fails. Not "something is red": a lane that has never passed is not a regression, and an unavailable lane is not a failure at all. A quality regression is printed but does not page anyone -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: exit_code returns 1 if there are any liveness regressions (c.regressed and severity liveness), else 0. It does not consider quality regressions or unavailable lanes.

claims.text: Injecting it is what lets the whole runner be tested with fakes and no network: the tests never construct an adapter, never touch a CLI and never open a socket.
claims.why: This claim about test behavior is not verifiable from this chunk; it depends on how tests use Lane. The code does show that ask is a callable injected, but the test claims are uncheckable.

claims.text: ``adapter`` is the seat ``ask`` was bound from, when there was one. It is carried for ONE reason: :func:`live_egress_lanes` has to hand something to :func:`session.live_egress_seats`, and a bare closure is not classifiable. Nothing in the runner reads it -- the canary still calls ``ask`` and only ``ask``, so a fake lane stays a fake lane.
claims.why: The claim that nothing in the runner reads adapter cannot be verified from this chunk; the runner is likely in another part of the file or another module. The code shows the field exists, but its usage is uncheckable.

claims.text: Resolve a vendor CLI to something ``CreateProcess`` can actually launch. On Windows a node CLI ships as an extensionless shell script beside a ``.exe``/``.cmd`` shim, and only the shim is launchable without a shell. Preferring the native ``.exe`` also skips the ``.cmd`` layer entirely -- the layer that truncated a multi-line argv and started all of this. (The prompt still goes on stdin regardless; the arrival probe is what proves that end to end rather than asserting it.) Returns ``name`` unchanged when nothing is found, so the spawn fails as ``not_on_path`` -> ``unavailable`` instead of guessing.
claims.why: The function iterates through .exe, .cmd, .bat, and name, returns the first found via shutil.which, and returns name unchanged if none found. The behavior matches the docstring.

claims.text: The council's data-notice preamble is for model-written evidence. A canary prompt is generated in this file and carries none -- and the preamble would sit AHEAD of the arrival nonce, destroying the head position that probe measures. So the probe body goes out verbatim.
claims.why: The method returns prompt unchanged, so the probe body goes out verbatim without preamble.

claims.text: Two overrides every canary adapter needs, and nothing else.
claims.why: The mixin defines exactly two methods: assemble and argv.

claims.text: The prompt still goes on stdin regardless; the arrival probe is what proves that end to end rather than asserting it.
claims.why: The claim about the arrival probe proving stdin end-to-end is not verifiable from this chunk; it depends on probe implementations and the overall runner.

observations.what: ProbeResult.__post_init__ validates status and severity against CANARY_STATUSES and SEVERITIES, but these constants are defined outside this chunk. If they are not exhaustive or if statuses are added later, validation could reject valid results.
ProbeResult.asked treats any status other than 'unavailable' as 'asked'. If a future status like 'skipped' or 'cancelled' is introduced, it would be misclassified as asked.

ProbeResult.to_record truncates reply to REPLY_TRIM, but REPLY_TRIM is not defined in this chunk. The exact truncation length is unverifiable, and if REPLY_TRIM is not defined, this would raise NameError at runtime.
default_lanes is cut off mid-function. The remainder of the function may contain logic that contradicts claims about lane construction or local detection, but it cannot be reviewed here.

_CanaryAdapterMixin.argv calls super().argv(model) and then resolves the executable. If the base adapter's argv returns an empty list, the function still works, but if it returns None or raises, the behavior is undefined.
_CanaryOllama overrides argv to return an empty list unconditionally, which may be correct for HTTP-only adapters, but if Ollama ever needs a CLI, this would silently break.
